instruction: Find the ACL Anthology Best Long Paper Award winners for 2019–2022 and enter their title, year, comma-separated authors, and PDF link into best_awards_acl.xlsx on the desktop.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires recording ACL Best Long Paper Award winners for 2019-2022 with title, year, authors, and PDF links. Evaluator extracts all four columns from the Excel file and verifies: (1) exactly 4 papers exist, (2) all titles are non-empty, (3) years are exactly 2019-2022, (4) all authors fields are non-empty, (5) all PDF links are valid aclanthology.org PDF URLs. Score is average of these 5 criteria. Custom getter extracts complete paper data as dict, metric performs comprehensive multi-field validation.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator provides comprehensive verification coverage across all 5 criteria
Getter correctly extracts all 4 required fields (title, year, authors, PDF link) from Excel file with proper header skipping

Metric verifies: (1) exactly 4 papers exist, (2) all titles non-empty, (3) years exactly {2019, 2020, 2021, 2022}, (4) all authors fields non-empty, (5) PDF links match valid aclanthology.org PDF URL pattern
Scoring logic is sound: returns average of 5 equally-weighted criteria scores, allowing partial credit
PDF link validation uses proper regex pattern 'https?://aclanthology\.org/.+\.pdf' (not just domain substring)
Edge case handling: properly handles empty papers list, None values, and missing fields
Postconfig is appropriate: activates LibreOffice window and saves file to ensure changes are persisted before evaluation
Minor issue: Year conversion in getter (line 42) uses str(year).isdigit() which could fail for float years from Excel, but unlikely to cause issues in practice
Minor issue: Authors validation accepts single authors without commas, which is technically valid but instruction says 'comma-delimited' (acceptable as edge case)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider more robust year conversion in getter: use isinstance(year, (int, float)) or try-except around int() conversion to handle Excel numeric types
Optional: Add explicit comma check for multi-author papers in authors validation if strict comma-delimited format is required
